title: How I Make Insane Motion Graphics with Opus 5.5 (Better than Fable or Astra)
creator: Jason Lee
summary: A walkthrough of making product-launch motion graphics with Claude Opus 5.5 (Claude Code), comparing it favourably to Fable and Astra. The creator starts from gathered visual references, prompts Opus for a first version, then does a dedicated issue-fixing pass and finishes edits in a tool called Motion OS Editor. A second launch video follows, then a cinematic piece where photoreal shots come from Higgsfield video/image models and are combined with the coded graphics.
what_is_shown: Two product-launch motion-graphics videos built from code by Opus 5.5, plus a cinematic video mixing AI-generated footage (Higgsfield: Seedream 5 Pro, Soul Cinema, Seedance 2.5) with the coded graphics. Exact rendering framework not named in the description.

techniques.name: Reference-first briefing
techniques.how: Collect existing motion references before prompting and feed them into the prompt so the model targets a concrete look rather than a vague style word.
techniques.quality_lever: Anchors art direction and pacing, avoiding the generic template look.

techniques.name: Dedicated fix pass after v1
techniques.how: Treat the first render as a draft, list visible defects, and prompt targeted corrections in a separate iteration.
techniques.quality_lever: Most polish comes from the critique-and-repair loop, not the first prompt.

techniques.name: Hybrid coded graphics plus generative footage
techniques.how: Use a video-generation model for photoreal or cinematic shots and keep typography, UI and diagram motion in code, then combine in an editor.
techniques.quality_lever: Each tool does what it is good at; code cannot produce photoreal people, generators cannot produce crisp exact text.

techniques.name: Post-edit in a timeline editor
techniques.how: Bring code-rendered output into an editor (Motion OS Editor) for final timing and assembly.
techniques.quality_lever: Human timing tweaks on top of agent output without re-prompting the whole piece.

prompting_patterns: Prompt includes collected references for the product-launch look (prompt text itself is sold/linked via thebreadcrumb.co, not read)
pipeline: find references -> prompt Opus 5.5 -> first version -> fix issues -> Motion OS Editor -> (second launch video) -> cinematic shots via Higgsfield -> final output
pitfalls: First version needs a dedicated fix pass (chapter 'Fixing Issues'); specific defects not readable from description
evidence: oEmbed + watch-page description and chapter list only; no transcript; linked prompts/repo (thebreadcrumb.co) truncated and not read.

title: OPUS 5.5 Just Killed Motion Graphics Designers!
creator: DopeShit
summary: Shows cartoon, watercolor-style motion graphics made by Claude Opus 5.5 writing JavaScript that paints every frame, using the community PDoomVideo music video (Clawd mascot) as the reference and the clawd-video skill as the reusable tool. The linked repos reveal the actual method: p5.js plus p5.brush scenes drawn as a pure function of time, rendered frame-by-frame in headless Chrome and encoded with FFmpeg, with synthesized audio.
what_is_shown: Hand-painted-looking 2D cartoon animation of the Clawd character with brush textures, comic fonts (Patrick Hand, Bangers, Permanent Marker), lyric-synced scenes and linked transitions.

techniques.name: Frame as pure function of t
techniques.how: scene.js draws rig, props, particles, light and paper grain from the time value alone; renderer seeks each frame and screenshots it.
techniques.quality_lever: Deterministic, re-renderable frames with exact timing regardless of capture speed.

techniques.name: Paint static layers once
techniques.how: Backgrounds and props are brush-painted a single time and cached, only moving parts are redrawn per frame.
techniques.quality_lever: Prevents watercolor texture from flickering/boiling between frames.

techniques.name: Story file as timeline
techniques.how: A story.js holds timed beats and audio cues that drive both visuals and a synthesized score.
techniques.quality_lever: Single source of truth keeps sound and picture locked.

techniques.name: Stills-first QA tooling
techniques.how: Render stills at chosen times, contact sheets, sampled full renders, and a motion checker that flags pose jumps before final output.
techniques.quality_lever: Catches layout and continuity errors cheaply before expensive full renders.

techniques.name: Agent-written storyboard and animation guide
techniques.how: In PDoomVideo Opus wrote a STORYBOARD.md and an ANIMATION_GUIDE.md to brief parallel subagents, one file per chapter.
techniques.quality_lever: Consistent style across long pieces produced in parallel; each transition designed to link to the next scene.

techniques.name: Squash-and-stretch rig
techniques.how: Character rigs documented in references and drawn procedurally with classic squash and stretch.
techniques.quality_lever: Cartoon appeal from animation principles rather than linear tweening.

prompting_patterns: Minimal creative direction: use the character design and give each lyric interesting visuals and transitions
Timed-beat prompts (e.g. 0-3 s: action) for clawd-video
Ask the model to look up an accurate reference for known characters before drawing
Instruct storyboard to use brushstrokes and connect every scene transition to the next
pipeline: idea -> story.js beats (+ storyboard/animation guide) -> paint static layers -> per-frame scene draw from t -> stills check -> headless Chrome frame capture (parallel workers, resumable) -> synth score on cues -> FFmpeg H.264/AAC MP4 (-16 LUFS) -> motion check
pitfalls: pageerror during render = JS error in story file
White halo around moving props when clip outline is too loose
First run slow while Chrome downloads
Texture flicker if painted layers are regenerated per frame
evidence: oEmbed + watch-page description (tools, links); READMEs of linked repos aadil6971/clawd-video and JohnHeibel/PDoomVideo. No video transcript.

title: Claude Opus 5.5 Killed Video Editing (For Real This Time)
creator: g russ
summary: Three tests of Opus 5.5 for video production: a Vox-style explainer motion graphic shown across three iterations, a PS1-era low-poly 3D casino reel in Three.js, and pure-JavaScript frame-by-frame animation inspired by Emergent Garden. Ends with a verdict on production use; the description mainly promotes a faceless-YouTube automation community.
what_is_shown: Vox-style explainer graphics (three versions side by side), procedural PS1 low-poly 3D animation, and generative JS animation.

techniques.name: Side-by-side iteration comparison
techniques.how: Keep successive versions of the same reel and compare them to judge what each revision fixed.
techniques.quality_lever: Makes improvement measurable and guides the next prompt.

techniques.name: Constrained retro 3D style
techniques.how: Ask for a deliberately low-fidelity look (PS1 low-poly) in Three.js, built procedurally.
techniques.quality_lever: A strong period constraint hides model weaknesses and produces a coherent aesthetic at low effort.

techniques.name: Named reference style (Vox)
techniques.how: Invoke a well-known explainer house style as the target.
techniques.quality_lever: Gives the model a dense shared vocabulary for layout, collage, and pacing.

prompting_patterns: Style-anchored prompts naming a known publication look (Vox) or era (PS1)
pipeline: prompt + setup -> iteration 1/2/3 -> compare -> (stated) production use
evidence: Watch-page description and chapter titles only; no transcript; no linked repo or write-up found.

title: 5 CODE-ONLY MOVIES Made By NEW AI Opus 5.5
creator: XplatformNEWS
summary: A compilation reposting five Opus 5.5 code-only animations from X creators the day after the model launched: a visual-design test, sketch-to-simulation, a JavaScript frame-by-frame short story, an imagined TikTok feed, and a John Wick action remake. It is a showcase, not a tutorial; no method is explained in the readable material.
what_is_shown: Five short code-rendered films covering visual design, a sketch turned into a simulation, hand-drawn-style JS frames, a social feed mock, and action choreography.

techniques.name: Sketch-to-simulation
techniques.how: Provide a rough sketch as input and have the model turn it into an animated simulation.
techniques.quality_lever: Visual input pins composition far better than text.

techniques.name: Per-frame JS drawing for narrative
techniques.how: Model writes code that draws each frame of a short story.
techniques.quality_lever: Full control of every frame enables character storytelling beyond tween presets.

title: How Claude Opus 5.5 Makes Motion Graphics (From One Prompt)
creator: Web3 Wesley
summary: Opus 5.5 builds a 15-second motion-design showreel from one short open-ended prompt, using HeyGen's open-source HyperFrames (HTML to video), GSAP and Three.js, and even writes its own JS synthesizer for sound effects. It took about 90 minutes on Claude Max; the same prompt in GPT 6 Astra via Codex was judged weaker on shapes, assets and animation.
what_is_shown: A 15 s showreel with shapes, a 3D bouncing ball, kinetic elements and self-generated SFX; a second example follows.

techniques.name: HTML composition with seekable timeline
techniques.how: HyperFrames compositions are HTML with clip elements carrying data-start/data-duration/data-track-index and a paused GSAP timeline registered on window.__timelines; the renderer seeks each frame in headless Chrome and encodes with FFmpeg.
techniques.quality_lever: Deterministic frame-exact output from plain HTML the model already writes well.

techniques.name: Mixed 2D/3D in one composition
techniques.how: Combine GSAP-driven DOM/SVG motion with a Three.js scene in the same timeline.
techniques.quality_lever: Adds depth and camera motion to otherwise flat kinetic graphics.

techniques.name: Model-synthesized sound design
techniques.how: Have the model write a small code synth for whooshes and hits timed to the visuals.
techniques.quality_lever: Audio-visual sync without licensed assets; makes reels feel finished.

techniques.name: Open-ended high-ambition prompt
techniques.how: A short brief asking the model to show off as a motion designer in a portfolio-style reel and go all out.
techniques.quality_lever: Lets the model choose a coherent concept; good for discovery before tightening constraints.

prompting_patterns: One-shot brief: 15 s showreel framed as the model's own motion-design resume, with an instruction to go all out
Same prompt A/B tested across models
pipeline: single prompt -> Opus writes HyperFrames composition (GSAP + Three.js) -> JS synth SFX -> preview -> render via headless Chrome + FFmpeg -> MP4 (~90 min agent time)
pitfalls: Long agent runtime (~90 min) for 15 s

HyperFrames docs note: GSAP from a blocked CDN breaks render (bundle locally); set start state with gsap.set before building timelines; animate transforms/opacity not layout props; deterministic render is Linux-only
evidence: Watch-page description and chapters; HyperFrames GitHub README and third-party write-ups (yuv.ai, roo.beehiiv) for mechanism. No transcript.

title: Introducing Open Intelligent UI | The Open-Source Alternative to ChatGPT's Intelligent UI
creator: CopilotKit
summary: CopilotKit launches an MIT-licensed generative-UI chat app where an agent answers each turn with text, a native component, or a custom sandboxed HTML/CSS/JS interface such as a rotatable 3D explainer, chart, calculator or map. It is about interactive in-app visuals rather than rendered video, but its skill structure, renderer decision matrix, and streaming sandbox are relevant to agent-produced animated explainers.
what_is_shown: Agent-generated interactive UIs: a 3D airplane explaining pitch/roll/yaw, algorithm visualizations, charts from tables, calculators, trip maps.

techniques.name: Renderer decision matrix
techniques.how: A routing step maps request type to medium: Three.js for 3D, canvas+JS for simulations, D3 for graphs, Chart.js for charts, Tone.js for audio.
techniques.quality_lever: Right engine per job instead of forcing everything through one library.

techniques.name: Streamed sandboxed HTML with morphing preview
techniques.how: Tool args stream css, html, then JS; the preview iframe is morphed with Idiomorph to avoid flicker before the final sandbox boots with shared design-system CSS and a CDN importmap.
techniques.quality_lever: Progressive reveal and consistent theming across all generated visuals.

techniques.name: Injected shared design system
techniques.how: Every generated iframe gets the same design-system CSS with automatic light/dark theming and responsive sizing.
techniques.quality_lever: Visual consistency without the model re-inventing styles each turn.

techniques.name: Progressive-disclosure skills
techniques.how: SKILL.md files (advanced-visualization, master-playbook, svg-diagrams) load on demand rather than bloating the system prompt.
techniques.quality_lever: Deep domain rules available when needed while keeping context lean.

prompting_patterns: Task-first system prompt plus on-demand skills; MCP prompt templates for widgets, SVG diagrams and advanced visualizations
pipeline: user request -> router picks renderer -> agent streams generateSandboxedUi (height, placeholders, css, html, js) -> morphing preview -> sandboxed iframe with design system -> optional follow-up via validated bridge
pitfalls: README warns weaker models produce broken layouts, missing interactivity or incomplete visuals
Host bridge calls must be validated
evidence: Watch-page description; GitHub README of CopilotKit/OpenIntelligentUI; everydev.ai tool page. No transcript.
